Lists the organization's identity providers and the email domains claimed for them. An organization signs in
through one provider per verified domain, so both are collections. Client secrets are write-only and are never
returned. An organization that has not set anything up yet responds 200 with empty lists.

403.description: Single sign-on is not enabled for the organization, or the caller is not an Admin

post.summary: Claim an email domain for SSO
post.description:
Claims an email domain and returns the DNS record that proves control of it. A claim is only a note to
ourselves: nothing is registered against the domain until verification succeeds, so claiming a domain neither
affects anyone's sign-in nor stops another organization claiming it first. A domain another organization has
already registered is refused with 409, before any DNS record is published.

403.description: Single sign-on is not enabled for the organization, or the caller is not an Admin

409.description: The domain is already registered to another organization

delete.summary: Release a claimed or verified domain
delete.description:
Drops a pending claim, or releases a verified domain so members on it sign in however they could before.
Refused with a 409 while the organization has a provider for the domain; remove the provider first. Idempotent.

403.description: Single sign-on is not enabled for the organization, or the caller is not an Admin

409.description: An identity provider is still connected to the domain

post.summary: Check the DNS record for a claimed domain
post.description:
Looks up the challenge TXT record. Verification is a poll, not a command: a missing or stale record is reported
as `verified: false` on a 200 rather than as an error, so a client can retry while DNS propagates. Verifying a
domain that lost its verification restores its provider, with enforcement off.

200.description: Current state of the domain after checking DNS

403.description: Single sign-on is not enabled for the organization, or the caller is not an Admin

404.description: The organization has not claimed the domain

409.description: Another organization verified the domain first

post.summary: Register an identity provider for a verified domain
post.description:
Registers an identity provider for one verified domain. `google` needs only the credentials and pins the login
to that Google Workspace domain; `microsoft` pins it to the Entra tenant in the issuer; `oidc` is the fallback
for any other provider and discovers its endpoints from the issuer's `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. The
domain must already be verified, and registering does not redirect anyone on its own: that is enabled
separately.

403.description: Single sign-on is not enabled for the organization, or the caller is not an Admin

409.description: The domain is not verified, or already has an identity provider

put.description:
Replaces the provider's credentials, and for `oidc` re-discovers its endpoints from the issuer. The domain it
serves and whether it is enforced are carried across unchanged, so rotating a client secret does not quietly
turn enforcement off. A provider whose domain stopped being verified is refused until the domain verifies again.

403.description: Single sign-on is not enabled for the organization, or the caller is not an Admin

404.description: The identity provider does not exist

409.description: The identity provider has no verified domain; verify the domain again first

delete.description:
Deletes the provider, so members on its domain fall back to the sign-in methods they had before. The domain
stays verified and can be given another provider. Idempotent.

403.description: Single sign-on is not enabled for the organization, or the caller is not an Admin

put.summary: Require members on this provider's domain to sign in through it
put.description:
Enabling sends every address on the provider's domain to it, leaving those members no other way in. Refused
with a 409 until the domain is verified. Disabling needs nothing, so the way out is always open.

403.description: Single sign-on is not enabled for the organization, or the caller is not an Admin

404.description: The identity provider does not exist

409.description: The domain of the identity provider is not verified

post.description:
Execute a single SQL query or a batch of queries against a PostgreSQL branch.

**Authentication:** send the branch's PostgreSQL connection string in the
`Connection-String` header. The control-plane API key (Bearer token) is
**not** accepted on the gateway host.

**Routing:** the target branch, region, and endpoint type are taken from the
hostname embedded in the connection string, which must match the request host.
See the `Connection-String` security scheme for the host format.

**Single query:** provide `query` (and optional `params`) at the top level.

**Batch:** provide `queries` as an array of query objects, or send the request body
as a JSON array. Batch queries execute within a single transaction.

**Errors:** PostgreSQL errors return 400 with their SQLSTATE in `code` and their
diagnostic fields. A 503 means the gateway could not reach the database: `08001`
when a connection cannot be established and `08006` when an established connection
fails. A 503 does not guarantee that replaying a write is safe: a connection failure
can leave its outcome unknown.

parameters.name: Array-Mode
parameters.description: When `true`, return rows as arrays instead of objects.

parameters.name: Raw-Text-Output
parameters.description: When `true`, return all values as strings without type conversion.

parameters.name: Batch-Isolation-Level
parameters.description: Transaction isolation level for batch queries.

parameters.name: Batch-Read-Only
parameters.description: When `true`, execute the batch transaction in read-only mode.

parameters.name: Batch-Deferrable
parameters.description: When `true`, execute the batch transaction in deferrable mode.

value.query: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = $1

batch.summary: Batch of queries in one transaction

single.summary: Result of the single query above

batch.summary: Result of the batch above, one entry per query

400.description: Invalid request, SQL error, query execution timeout, or a result larger than the 10MB response limit

403.description: Client IP is not allowed by the branch IP filter

404.description: Branch not found, it may have been deleted

409.description: Branch is hibernated, reactivate it before running queries

503.description: Gateway connection to the database failed

504.description: Timed out connecting to the database

get.description:
Upgrade to a WebSocket connection that proxies the PostgreSQL wire protocol.
The client sends and receives PostgreSQL protocol messages over binary WebSocket frames.

**Authentication:** the same branch connection string credential as the
HTTP SQL endpoint is used, but it is supplied via the PostgreSQL startup
message inside the wire protocol rather than an HTTP header. The
control-plane API key (Bearer token) is not accepted.

400.description: Bad request — unable to upgrade connection

post.description:
Handle a single JSON-RPC 2.0 message from an MCP client, per the MCP
[Streamable HTTP transport](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports).

The server is stateless: every request is self-contained and carries the caller's
credential, so there is no session to establish or resume. `GET` and `DELETE` on this
path return `405 Method Not Allowed`.

**Requests** (messages with an `id`) are answered with the JSON-RPC response, either as
`application/json` or as a `text/event-stream` carrying the response and any notifications
emitted while it runs. Requests must accept both. **Notifications and responses**
(messages without an `id`) are answered with `202 Accepted` and an empty body.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Must list both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`.

parameters.name: MCP-Protocol-Version
parameters.description:
Protocol revision negotiated during `initialize`, echoed on every subsequent request.
Omitted on the `initialize` request itself.

initialize.summary: Start a session and learn the server's capabilities

toolsCall.summary: Result of the tool call above

schema.description: Server-sent events, each `data` field holding one JSON-RPC message.

202.description: Notification or response accepted; no body is returned

400.description: Malformed message, unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version`, or an `Accept` header missing one of the required media types

WWW-Authenticate.description: Bearer challenge pointing at the protected resource metadata, per RFC 9728.

put.description:
Create or update an installation. Vercel sends this when a customer
installs (or re-sends it idempotently). The acting account is taken from
the signed token claims, not this body. There is one installation per
Vercel team, and an installation can own many Xata organizations.

204.description:
Installation created or updated. No body. (Vercel's contract also
allows a 200 with an installation-level billingPlan/notification
body; Xata does not use installation-level billing plans.)

delete.description:
Begin uninstalling an installation. The installation is marked
'deleting' so billing can finalize before being soft-deleted; the 204
defers final deletion to Vercel's 24-hour window. (Vercel's contract
also allows a 200 with {"finalized": true} for immediate deletion;
Xata always finalizes asynchronously.)

204.description: Uninstall accepted; deletion finalizes asynchronously. No body.

get.summary: List billing plans for a product
get.description:
Return the product's available billing plans, rendered into Vercel's
billingPlan shape. Vercel calls this to show plans when a customer creates
a resource; it may be called before any installation exists, so the signed
token can carry no installation or account id. Plans are billing SKUs only
and do not change Xata entitlements (every Vercel org is T2).

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description: Opaque metadata forwarded by Vercel.

get.description:
Return a provisioned resource. Scoped to the installation in the signed
token; a resource owned by another installation is reported as not found.

delete.description:
Deprovision a resource (its Xata project and branches) and mark the
tracking records deleting. Vercel calls this when a customer removes a
resource. Idempotent: a resource already being torn down is deprovisioned
again harmlessly; a resource that no longer exists returns 404.

post.description:
Create a resource (a Xata project and its branches) and return it with
the connection secrets. Vercel calls this when a customer creates a
resource. Idempotent when an Idempotency-Key header is sent: a retry with
the same key returns the existing resource unchanged, and reusing the key
with a different body is a conflict (409). Without the header there is no
stable key, so each call provisions a new resource.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
A stable key Vercel sends to make retries safe. A repeat with the same
key returns the existing resource; reusing it with a different body is a
conflict (409). Optional — without it each call provisions a new resource.

200.description: The provisioned resource, with connection secrets.

Because of this, restore points older than retentionPeriod are sometimes available, but how far back they go depends on the backup schedule and is not guaranteed.
